stemBlocks.value: Make s the subject of the formula t = s/5.
Think first: Here s is divided by 5, so multiplication is what releases it.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p055-q04 from workbook page 55.

solutionSteps.instruction: Identify what is being done to s.

whyThisWorks.value: Dividing by 5 is undone by multiplying by 5, and applying that multiplication to both sides keeps the formula true. The 5 on the left becomes a multiplier of t, giving s = 5t. In words, s is five times whatever t is — the same statement as t being one fifth of s.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing s = t/5, repeating the division instead of reversing it.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing s = t/5, repeating the division instead of reversing it.

commonErrors.misconception: Multiplying only the left-hand side by 5.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Multiplying only the left-hand side by 5.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing s = t + 5 by treating the division as an addition.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing s = t + 5 by treating the division as an addition.

examTip.value: A denominator moves to the other side as a multiplier, and a multiplier moves across as a denominator. Say that rule to yourself before you write the line.
